title: Uniform compact approximation slices of accessible infinity functors
statement:
Use the infinity-category and universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], the filteredness and compactness conventions of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], and $\kappa$-cofinality as defined in [lem-coef-infinity-filtered-cofinal-pullback]. Let $\{\mathcal C_v\}$ be a finite family of accessible infinity categories and let $\{F_e:\mathcal C_{s(e)}\to\mathcal C_{t(e)}\}$ be a finite family of accessible functors between them. Here accessible for a functor means preserving small $\rho$-filtered colimits for some infinite regular $\rho$.

There exist infinite regular cardinals $\kappa<\tau$ in the smaller universe, with $\tau$ uncountable, having all the following properties simultaneously. Each $\mathcal C_v$ is locally small and is both $\kappa$-accessible and $\tau$-accessible; each $F_e$ preserves small $\kappa$-filtered and small $\tau$-filtered colimits and carries $\tau$-compact objects to $\tau$-compact objects. The full subcategory $\mathcal C_v^\tau$ of $\tau$-compact objects is essentially small, that is, equivalent to a small infinity category.

For $c\in\mathcal C_v$, let $K_v(c)=(\mathcal C_v^\tau)_{/c}$ denote the full subcategory of $\mathcal C_v{}_{/c}$ consisting of arrows with $\tau$-compact source; the slice has arrows into $c$ as objects and coherent commuting triangles as morphisms, retaining all higher compatibilities. It is essentially small and $\tau$-filtered, its source projection $K_v(c)\to\mathcal C_v$ has the canonical colimit $c$, and it admits all $\tau$-small $\kappa$-filtered colimits, computed in $\mathcal C_v{}_{/c}$. For each $F_e$ and $c\in\mathcal C_{s(e)}$, the functor
$$K_{s(e)}(c)\longrightarrow K_{t(e)}(F_e(c)),\qquad(d\to c)\longmapsto(F_e(d)\to F_e(c))$$
preserves those $\tau$-small $\kappa$-filtered colimits and is $\kappa$-cofinal.
